intent_snapshot.goal: Deliver explicit claimless SQLite migration, remove obsolete authority and relocation writers, and prove dual-host/worktree/batch/tracker and package readiness for one coordinated major release.

acceptance.assertion: Explicit migration refuses active tasks or recoverable old batches, preserves raw historical evidence, imports into a verified temporary SQLite database and recovers interrupted publication without dual writes; schema mismatch, consistent restore and worktree rebinding reject unsafe access.

Legacy JSON authority writers, byte-CAS journals and duplicate claim/tombstone/relocation runtime paths are removed; historical audit remains readable solely as evidence, with the read-only importer carrying its next-major removal milestone.
Batch recovery binds the approved child to its exact run, preserves single-task ownership/base/budget/critical restrictions and requires the correct exported terminal attachment before commit.

Packaged Claude and Pi consumers remain coherent with the new runtime and documented support floor; the checked-in bundle matches the implementation and required release artifacts contain no legacy fallback.

Tracker terminal projection validates the assigned exact run before changing an Issue; another run with the same task_id cannot close it, and shared-worktree publication remains idempotent without changing canonical authority.

attestations.summary: Verified the manifest digest, the commit's single parent, its tree and every changed path object; the migration, recovery and evidence-preservation paths and their contracts show no blocking defect, and A1-A5 rely on the embedded Kernel QA outcomes.

findings.summary: The explicit SQLite importer named by the slice does not exist, so a migratable legacy workspace cannot be migrated.

evidence.trigger: A legacy workspace with no active owner and complete committed terminal evidence is diagnosed as migration_required; migrateLegacyLayout returns invalid instead of importing into a temporary SQLite database and publishing it.

findings.summary: The legacy relocation writer path is still live, contrary to the retirement this slice claims.

evidence.trigger: A workspace carrying a valid storage-layout-migration.json marker still replays relocations and deletes legacy files inside the dual-locked recovery branch.

findings.summary: The new migration has no reachable public entry point: probeKernelStore throws on any retired tasks directory before kernel.ts reaches migrateLegacyLayout, and v4_runtime.ts still rejects migrate.

evidence.trigger: A worktree has no SQLite store and holds a valid terminal .imm/state/tasks/<task-id>.json plus its matching terminal proof; the operator runs imm-kernel to migrate or author an intent.

findings.summary: candidateReady is treated as an exemption from the evidence-commit check, and git status cannot see ignored untracked copies, so publication can delete the only copy of the historical bytes.

evidence.trigger: A verified candidate store exists but was not published; the committed audit copies are then deleted from HEAD while the legacy sources stay, and the migration runs again.

findings.summary: Cleanup only runs when remaining tasks exist, so an interrupted final deletion leaves an orphan proof that keeps the layout invalid while the retry reports success.

evidence.trigger: The store and receipt are published; the last legacy record was deleted but its proof was not, and the process exits before removing it.

findings.summary: Cleanup ignores the other retired artifacts the inspector still reads, so a migrated worktree keeps an invalid layout and the ledger never reaches the legacy audit path.

evidence.trigger: An owner-free retired worktree holds a valid terminal task plus a committed .imm/memory/current_iteration.json with runtime_status idle, or a .imm/tasks/.workspace.lock; the migration runs after the audit evidence is committed.

findings.summary: Review returned this acceptance boundary twice; a durable replan is required.
